haiku-low.q1: After the message and outbox row commit (step 2), the gateway acks (step 3) with msg_id and seq. The ack does not wait for fan-out.
haiku-low.q2: The sender gets an error. No message or outbox row is written, so nobody receives it. The retry must reuse the same msg_id, which the unique key uses to prevent a second copy.
haiku-low.q3: When its Presence entry expires, 30 seconds after the last heartbeat. Heartbeats are every 10 seconds. A clean socket close deletes the entry immediately.
haiku-low.q4: The worker treats the recipient as offline. It writes the Offline Inbox entry first, then requests a push notification.
haiku-low.q5: It is logged and ignored. It is not retried and never touches the inbox, because the inbox entry was already written durably.
haiku-low.q6: Missed messages are sent in (conversation, seq) order from the inbox. The client drops any msg_id it has already seen.
haiku-low.q7: The outbox row commits in the same transaction as the message. After a crash, the relay queues any unpublished row on its next poll, so it still reaches everyone.
haiku-low.q8: In the Presence Registry, which maps user to gateway node with a 30-second TTL. Expiry removes an entry when heartbeats stop. A clean close deletes it at once.
haiku-low.q9: The worker asks the recipient's gateway to deliver. The gateway pushes over the WebSocket and waits up to 5 seconds for the client's ack, which confirms receipt.
haiku-low.q10: In the Offline Inbox. The worker writes it before any push, when the recipient is offline. The entry is removed when the client acks it on reconnect, or expires after 30 days.
haiku-low.q11: The Offline Inbox, sorted by (conversation, seq), for pointers. The gateway then fetches each message body from the Message Store.
haiku-low.q12: The queue job is not marked done, so it is redelivered and processed again. Recipients already served may receive a duplicate, which clients drop by msg_id.

sonnet.q1: After the gateway commits the message and outbox row in one transaction (step 3). The ack carries msg_id and seq. It never waits on fan-out.
sonnet.q2: The sender gets an error. No one receives the message (no message and no outbox row exist). The retry must carry the same msg_id, which hits the UNIQUE(conversation, msg_id) key.
sonnet.q3: After 30 seconds with no heartbeat, when the Presence Registry entry expires (heartbeats come every 10s and refresh the entry).
sonnet.q4: The worker treats the recipient as offline and takes the offline path: it writes an inbox entry (8b) and then requests a push. The client may see the message twice and drops repeats by msg_id.
sonnet.q5: Nothing happens beyond logging. The failure is ignored, never retried, and does not touch the inbox. The inbox entry is already durable.
sonnet.q6: In seq order within each conversation (inbox sorted by (conv, seq)). The client drops any msg_id it has already seen.
sonnet.q7: The outbox row was committed in the same transaction as the message, so it stays unpublished. The relay polls unpublished rows and queues it on its next poll, so the acknowledged message still gets fanned out.
sonnet.q8: In the Presence Registry (user -> node). Each entry has a 30s TTL refreshed by 10s heartbeats, so it expires on its own if heartbeats stop. It is deleted on a clean socket close.
sonnet.q9: The worker asks the recipient's gateway node to deliver. That gateway pushes the message over the recipient's WebSocket (9a). The client's ack (10a) confirms arrival, sent back to the gateway and then the worker. The gateway waits up to 5 seconds for it.
sonnet.q10: In the Offline Inbox, as pointers (user, conv, seq, msg_id) with a 30-day TTL. An entry is written by the worker on the offline path (step 8b), before any push is requested. Entries are removed when the client acks the message after reconnect (the gateway deletes it), or when the 30-day TTL expires.
sonnet.q11: The gateway reads the user's Offline Inbox, sorted by (conv, seq), then fetches each message body from the Message Store and streams it.
sonnet.q12: The queue job is not marked done, so it is redelivered and processed again. Recipients already served may get a duplicate, which clients drop by msg_id.
